meta.author: Governance as Code

rules.sublabel: one source, read by AI and tools

cop.title: Red Hat good practices
cop.description: The community baseline for writing Ansible. Used as published and pinned to a version; never copied or modified.

aiforge.title: ai-forge
aiforge.description: Skills that give AI assistants Ansible know-how: scaffolding, writing content, tests, reviews.

aapskills.title: aap-skills
aapskills.description: Skills to operate Ansible Automation Platform through its MCP server. Read-only by default.

adrs.title: Decisions (ADRs)
adrs.description: Every company rule starts as a decision: context, decision, consequences, who approved it. Only what differs from the community.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Each decision becomes one machine-readable rule. AI assistants and checkers read the same source.

repomap.title: Repository map
repomap.description: Which repositories reach production. It decides which rules apply — not the person asking. Unlisted repositories are treated as production.

exceptions.title: Exceptions
exceptions.description: When a project cannot comply: narrow scope, approved by the rule owner, with an expiry date. Expired exceptions stop working automatically.

ruletests.title: Rule tests
ruletests.description: Each automatic rule has examples that must pass and must fail. They already caught three defects in our own rules.

skills.title: Installed once
skills.description: One setup per repository installs the modes and the community skills, pinned, for Claude Code or Cursor's own chat (gac-setup.sh --assistant cursor).

auditor.title: Auditor
auditor.description: Reviews existing automation against community and company rules. Every finding says which rule and who decided it.

builder.title: Builder
builder.description: Creates or modernizes automation. Agrees the success contract first, then builds until every check passes.

librarian.title: Librarian
librarian.description: Turns needs into proposed decisions and rules, measuring their impact. It never approves.

operator.title: Operator
operator.description: Checks jobs and diagnoses failures in AAP. Read-only first; any change needs explicit confirmation.

contract.title: Success contract
contract.description: What will count as success, approved by a person before building: what must stay the same, what changes, how it is checked.

slots.title: Plug-in points
slots.description: New AI tools appear every week. Each one plugs into one of eight fixed points through a decision (ADR). The ACME instance adopts all eight; the live demo setup verifies the required ones — Slots active: 6/8 (Integrations and Input need an AAP endpoint / optional tools). Includes a guardrail that checks every edit the AI makes.

legacy.title: Legacy role (2017)
legacy.description: Does not load on current Ansible, sets each password to the user name, and its password policy has never worked on modern systems.

modern.title: Modernized role
modern.description: 0 findings, no default password, idempotent: a second run changes nothing.

prodcoll.title: Production collection
prodcoll.description: Production → an automated test is required (rule R-TEST-001).

labcoll.title: Lab collection
labcoll.description: Lab → no automated test required. Same checker, no shortcuts.

fwrepos.title: Firewall repositories
fwrepos.description: One legacy repository needs a forbidden collection until its migration: it has an exception until 31 March 2027.

checker.title: Checker
checker.description: The same automatic check for people, AI assistants, pre-commit and CI: community rules plus your rules. In the live demo it also runs from the terminal with no AI involved.

testplat.title: Test platform
testplat.description: Disposable containers declared by your governance, so tests run the same way everywhere.

ci.title: CI gate
ci.description: Blocks the merge when a rule is broken — even if an AI assistant ignored its instructions.

steps.text: Red Hat publishes good practices for Ansible.
ai-forge gives AI assistants Ansible know-how.
aap-skills lets AI assistants operate the platform.
But every company already has its own way of working…
…its naming, forbidden collections, approvals. No community base knows them.
Without governance, every team and every AI assistant improvises.
Result: many ways of doing the same thing, and no one can prove which is right.

layers.label: 1 · Community first, your rules on top

steps.text: Layer 0: the community baseline, used as published and pinned.
People decide only what is different — and record why.
Each decision becomes one rule, in one place.
The repository map decides where each rule applies: production is stricter.
A project that cannot comply gets an exception: narrow, approved, with an expiry date.
Every automatic rule has tests that prove it works.
Community baseline + your differences = the rules that apply here.

harness.label: 2 · The AI assistant and the trusted zone

steps.text: Every AI assistant gets the same skills, installed once.
New AI tools plug into eight fixed points. The method stays the same when tools change; the live demo activates the required slots (6/8).
The assistant reads only the rules that apply to the task.
While it works, a guardrail checks every edit and shows the AI what to fix — on the spot.
Whatever the assistant produces goes through the checker.
The CI gate blocks anything that breaks a rule — even if the AI ignored its instructions.
Guidance lives in the assistant; the guarantee lives in the gates.
Set up once per repository: modes and community skills, pinned.
/audit — review what already exists.
/build — create or modernize automation.
/librarian — propose a rule or an exception. People approve.
/operate — check jobs in the platform. Read-only first.
The Operator works only through the platform's official interface.
Same modes for every company; only the governance changes.
Start from the community; never fork it.
Your company decides only the differences — with traceability.
AI assistants follow the same rules as people.
Success is agreed before building.
Gates guarantee it — with or without AI.
New tools plug in without redesigning anything.
Part 1 · Clone the 2017 role (silvinux/ansible-manage-users).
Add the company governance as a pinned submodule (ACME) and AGENTS.md.
Decisions, rules, exceptions and the repository map — one instance.
Install the harness once: modes, skills, guardrail. Slots active: 6/8.
Works the same in Claude Code or Cursor's own chat.
What changed: submodule + AGENTS.md to commit; skills and hook installed locally.
Part 2 · Audit the role under ACME (new chat).
While it works: Auditor declares mode and resolves ACME rules for prod.
Findings cite every rule and decision. It changes nothing and asks before building.
Part 3 · Build: one /build paste (contract approved in the prompt) — it rewrites the role.
While it builds: rewrite under company rules, checker loop until 0 block findings.
Guardrail test: ask the AI to write a forbidden community.general task.
The guardrail answers at once (R-COLL-001 / ADR-0005); the AI fixes it.
The gate without AI: same ansible-lint CI would run — from the role root.
0 findings. Guidance lived in the assistant; the gate still proves it.

ex02.label: 5 · EX-02 — Create a collection (prod vs lab)

steps.text: EX-02 · Two requests: a production collection and a lab collection.
The Builder creates the production collection.
While it scaffolds: ansible-creator, then ACME pointer + checker hook + CI gate.
The repository map classifies it as production.
Production → an automated test is required, and it runs.
The Builder creates the lab collection.
While it scaffolds the lab collection: same Builder, different map entry.
The repository map classifies it as lab → no test required.
The lab collection passes the same checker: no shortcuts.
So does the production collection.
Requirements come from the map — never from who asks.
EX-03 · Security asks: production must not use a community collection without support.
While it works: Librarian checks L0 first, then drafts ADR + rule + lint rule.
The Librarian measures the impact on every repository in the map.
Only 1 of 6 repositories is affected.
It drafts the decision and the rule…
…with tests that prove the rule, written first.
People approve the decision.
The decision becomes a rule.
While the Builder drafts: watch for community.general — the new rule must catch it.
An AI-written draft uses the forbidden collection…
…and the checker blocks it.
While it rewrites: supported modules only (ansible.builtin / posix / certified).
The Builder rewrites it with supported modules.
The legacy firewall repository gets an exception until March 2027.
When it expires, the gate blocks again — automatically.

ex04.label: 7 · EX-04 — Plug tools into the harness

steps.text: EX-04 · A team wants a new tool: shorter command output for the AI.
The Librarian drafts an adoption decision: what it touches, how it is pinned, what it could conflict with, how to verify and remove it.
People approve it.
It plugs into the Input slot. Nothing else changes.
One setup per repository installs and verifies every adopted tool: 8 of 8 slots active.
While setup runs: each slot pinned, applied, verified — narrate the counters.
Test in a fresh AI session: it writes a forbidden module, on purpose…
While the agent writes the forbidden task: wait for the postToolUse hook.
…and the guardrail answers at once, with the rule and the decision behind it.
The AI fixes it before anything reaches CI. The CI gate still proves it.
Evolution: expired exceptions now fail the governance checks automatically.
Every new tool: one slot, one decision. The method stays the same.
Validation · A clean repository, set up once.
A fresh assistant runs an audit with only the installed skills.
While it audits: only installed skills — no coaching from the operator.
It follows the method — and finds things we had missed.
It also exposed three defects in the method itself.
We fixed them, writing the tests first.
A fresh assistant modernizes the role.
While it builds: same contract discipline — watch for lessons on where tests run.
Its role works: the second run changes nothing.
Its own test could not run in that session — lesson: tests must run where they are written.
Second fresh session, all eight slots active: the guardrail fired live and the AI fixed the code at once.
The method improves with every use (Evolution).
